name: Chalk-Hound

Traits.name: Pressed to the Wall
Traits.text: While the chalk-hound is pressed flat against plaster, plasterboard, or cut stone, it has Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks to hide there, and it leaves no silhouette—unless it chooses to move.
Traits.clause: While the chalk-hound is pressed flat against plaster, plasterboard, or cut stone, it has Advantage on Dexterity (Stealt
Traits.expresses: dragging prey through the wall into the hollow behind it

Traits.name: Incorporeal Movement
Traits.text: The chalk-hound can move through other creatures and objects as if they were Difficult Terrain. It takes 5 (1d10) Force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

Traits.name: Sunlight Sensitivity
Traits.text: While in sunlight, the chalk-hound has Disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls.

Actions.name: Multiattack
Actions.text: The chalk-hound makes two Chitin Claw attacks. It can replace one attack with a use of Wall Drag.

Actions.name: Chitin Claw
Actions.text: *Melee Attack Roll:* +8, reach 5 ft. 27 (5d8 + 5) Slashing damage.

Actions.name: Wall Drag
Actions.text: *Strength Saving Throw*: DC 16, one Medium or smaller creature the chalk-hound is touching. *Failure:* 14 (4d6) Slashing damage, and the chalk-hound drags the target up to 15 feet through a wall, floor, or other solid object it can pass through; the target emerges Prone in the nearest unoccupied space at the far side. If no such space is within 15 feet, the target is not moved. *Success:* Half damage only.
Actions.gmQuote: drags you back out through them

lore: A chalk-hound is what becomes of a starving predator that laired too long in the crack between a wall and its plaster, its hide grown to chalky chitin that no longer respects the boundary of the room, and it wants one thing — a living body pulled into the space behind the wall where nothing can follow.
